explain.say: Most liquids get denser as they cool. Water does too, but only down to about 4 degrees Celsius; below that it expands again. So in autumn, cooling surface water sinks until the whole lake is about 4 degrees.

faq.q: Why is water heaviest at 4 degrees?
faq.a: As water cools its molecules slow and pack closer, but below about 4 degrees Celsius they start forming the open structure of ice, which takes more room. So water is densest at about 4 degrees.

faq.q: Why is ice lighter than water?
faq.a: When water freezes, its molecules link up with hydrogen bonds into an open six-sided pattern with lots of space. The same mass takes up about 9 percent more room, so ice is less dense and floats.

faq.q: How do fish survive in frozen lakes?
faq.a: The ice on top insulates the water below, which stays liquid at about 4 degrees Celsius near the bottom. Fish slow down in the cold and need less food and oxygen until spring.

faq.q: Why do pipes burst in winter?
faq.a: When water in a pipe freezes it expands by about 9 percent, pushing hard on the pipe walls, which can crack them.

faq.q: What would happen if ice sank?
faq.a: Lakes and seas would freeze from the bottom up, and in cold places they could freeze solid, killing much of the life in them. Floating ice is one reason life survives cold winters.
asks: Why is it important that ice floats?

facts: Fresh water is densest at about 4 degrees Celsius.
Ice is about 9 percent less dense than liquid water.

quiz.say: In winter, what temperature is the water at the bottom of a deep, frozen lake?
quiz.show: Under the ice, the bottom of a deep lake is about…
quiz.why: Water is densest at about 4 degrees, so that water sinks and stays at the bottom while the ice above insulates it.

wrong.1: Liquid fresh water cannot be that cold, and the ice lid keeps the deep water much warmer.
wrong.2: Deep lakes do not freeze solid, because ice floats and insulates the water beneath.
